page: Vultr vhp-4c-12gb-amd is a High Performance family virtual server featuring an x86_64 AMD EPYC CPU with 4 shared vCPUs, mapped to 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The processor operates at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz and includes 16 MB of L3 cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1d cache. It is equipped with 12.0 GB of system memory, providing 3.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled with a 260 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates average performance for standard computational tasks, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests scoring 2427.57 and 9526.81 respectively. The memory subsystem demonstrates an average read-only bandwidth of 380.64 GB/sec for small cached blocks, but drops to a weak 24.31 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, alongside a weak write bandwidth of 20.91 GB/sec. PassMark CPU encryption tests show average performance at 3738.58, while database operations and overall memory scores are categorized as poor. For lightweight machine learning, LLM text generation using a small 135M model achieves an average speed of 87.51 tokens/sec, though prompt processing remains weak at 237.04 tokens/sec.

Given its shared CPU allocation and weak-to-average benchmark profile, this server offers a cost-efficient entry point for workloads that require moderate memory and fast local NVMe storage without demanding sustained, dedicated CPU performance. It is suitable for basic web serving, development environments, lightweight background workers, and small-scale database testing where resource density is prioritized over raw compute throughput.
description: Vultr vhp-4c-12gb-amd is a High Performance virtual server configured with 4 shared AMD EPYC vCPUs, 12.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 260 GB NVMe SSD. Operating on the x86_64 architecture at 2.0 GHz, this instance delivers average CPU performance in stress-ng benchmarks but exhibits weak memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks and poor database operation scores. It supports hardware-accelerated cryptography via AES and SHA_NI flags. Lacking a dedicated GPU, it is best suited for workloads with moderate resource requirements, such as static web serving, software development environments, and lightweight background processing tasks where local NVMe storage speed is beneficial but dedicated CPU cores are not strictly required.
